title: Predict: loops
prompt: Trace counting loops, a post-test loop, a loop inside a loop, and an unsigned test, and say what a register holds when each one ends.

predictions.code:
mov w19, 0          // sum
    mov w20, 1          // i
    b test
body:
    add w19, w19, w20
    add w20, w20, 2
test:
    cmp w20, 9
    b.le body
predictions.question: What does w19 hold when the loop ends? Answer in decimal.
predictions.explanation: The jump to test checks i before the first pass. The body runs for i = 1, 3, 5, 7 and 9, adding each one to the sum, and the loop stops when i reaches 11. 1 + 3 + 5 + 7 + 9 = 25.
predictions.hint: List the values i takes while the test i <= 9 still holds.

predictions.code:
mov w19, 0          // passes
    mov w20, 12         // i
again:
    add w19, w19, 1
    add w20, w20, 1
    cmp w20, 10
    b.lt again
predictions.question: This loop has no jump to its test before the first pass. How many passes does it make, as counted in w19? Answer in decimal.
predictions.explanation: Nothing is tested until the body has run, so the first pass always happens: w19 becomes 1 and i becomes 13. The test 13 < 10 fails, so there is no second pass. A pre-test loop with the same test would make none.
predictions.hint: The body runs before the first compare.

predictions.code:

loop:

    add w20, w20, 1

predictions.question: How many passes does the loop make, as counted in w19? Answer in decimal.
predictions.explanation: lo compares as unsigned. After the first pass i is -1, which as a word is 0xffffffff, the largest unsigned value there is, so it is not below 2 and the loop stops. The signed b.lt would run four passes, for i = -2, -1, 0 and 1.
